questions.question:
**In the following question, some part of the sentence may have errors. Find out which part of the sentence has an error and select the appropriate option. If a sentence is free from error, select 'No Error'.** 

Industries should regularly check (1)/ if their machines are emitting (2)/ smoke within permission limits. (3)/ No error (4)
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **3**

***__Key Points__**

Reading the above sentence we find that: 

__
 
• In the given sentence the word **permission **which is used is a noun. 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• Here the noun **permission **is used to describe another noun **limits**. 
 
• This is not grammatically correct, as only an **adjective **can modify a **noun**. 
 
• Therefore to modify the noun **limits **we should use an adjective. 
 
• Therefore we should replace the noun **permission **with the adjective **permissible**
 
• Thus the error lies in the 3rd part of the sentence. 

Therefore the correct answer is **3**

The correct sentence will be: Industries should regularly check if their machines are emitting smoke within **permissible **limits. *

**In the following question, the sentence given with blank to be ﬁlled in with an appropriate word. Select the correct alternative out of the four and indicate it by selecting the appropriate option.**

questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Infirm**.

Reading the given sentence we find that it is talking about the old man. 

Let's look at the meaning of the given words. 

 
• **confirm**: establish the truth or correctness. 
 
• **infirm**: physically or mental weakness due to old age. 
 
• **infer**: deduce or conclude from evidence and reasoning. 
 
• **luxurious**: elegant, extremely comfortable, grand. 

Thus from the given meaning, we find that the correct answer is **infirm**. 

The correct sentence will be: *The old man was **infirm **and poor. *

questions.question:
**Rearrange the parts of the sentence in the correct order. ** 

“Make in India” is not a mere 

P: accomplished by a single-minded 

Q: slogan but a mission to be 

R: commitment towards new processes
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **QPR**. 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

Reading the given sentences we find that:

 
• **Mere **means **small **and is an **adjective**. So the next part of the sentence should start with a **noun**. 
 
• Out of the given segments, **P **starts with the word **accomplished** which is a verb and cannot follow the adjective **mere**.
 
• Segment **P **cannot be the last one either as it ends with **single-minded** which is again an adjective. 
 
• If segment **R **is considered as the starting segment then it will yield a sentence that is not contextually or grammatically coherent. 
 
• Therefore segment **Q **can be the only starting segment that is contextually and grammatically correct. 
 
• The adjective in part **P **should be followed by yet another **noun**.
 
• The adjective **single-minded **will be followed by the noun **commitment** making segment **R **the last part. 

Therefore the correct answer is **QPR.**

The correct sentence will be: *Make in India is not a mere slogan but a mission to be accomplished by a single-minded commitment towards new processes. *

questions.question:
**In the following question, out of the four alternatives, select the alternative which best expresses the meaning of the idiom/phrase. ** 

A little bird told me

options.text: Have a strong network of spies from where you get reliable information from which you can proﬁt.
Used to indicate that the speaker knows something but chooses to keep the identity of their informant secret.
A secret which is known by everybody.
A person unknowingly letting out a secret.

questions.solution:
The alternative that best expresses the meaning of the idiom/phrase "A little bird told me" is:

**Used to indicate that the speaker knows something but chooses to keep the identity of their informant secret.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The idiom "A little bird told me" is commonly used to indicate that the speaker has obtained information or a secret from an undisclosed source, but they prefer not to reveal the identity of the person who informed them. It implies that the information came to them in a secretive or indirect manner.
 
• Option 2 captures the essence of this meaning by emphasizing the secrecy of the source while acknowledging that the speaker is aware of certain information without explicitly revealing how they came to know it.
 
• Therefore, option 2) Used to indicate that the speaker knows something but chooses to keep the identity of their informant secret is the best choice that expresses the meaning of the idiom/phrase.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• ** Have a strong network of spies from where you get reliable information from which you can profit.**

 
 
• This option suggests having a network of spies or informants to gather reliable information that can be used for personal gain or profit. While it touches on the aspect of obtaining information, it does not capture the idea of receiving information in a secretive or indirect manner, which is the main characteristic of the idiom.
 
 
 
• **A secret which is known by everybody.**
 
 
• This option suggests that the information is a widely known secret. However, the idiom "A little bird told me" implies the opposite, that the information is known only to a select few or in a secretive manner, rather than being widely known.
 
 
 
• **A person unknowingly letting out a secret.**
 
 
• This option suggests that the idiom refers to someone unintentionally revealing a secret. However, the idiom actually implies that the speaker intentionally received information but chooses to keep the identity of the informant secret. It does not convey the sense of accidental disclosure.

B: effects of all languages on one another 

C: call it an abomination despite 

35:T

Reading the above sentence we find that: 

__
 
• Compelled to which means forced to should be followed by a verb. 
 
• Out of the given sentences, only C starts with a verb i.e call it an abomination.

Thus the correct answer is CAB. 

The correct sentence will be: *I am compelled to call it an abomination despite being fully cognizant of the rich effects of all languages on one another.*
